blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights this 2012 paper by Krizhevsky et al. as a landmark contribution to deep learning, noting its surprisingly accessible readability. The authors demonstrate that an eight-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) can achieve state-of-the-art results on the ImageNet Large-Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (ILSVRC), significantly outperforming prior methods with top-1 and top-5 error rates of 37.5% and 17.0%, respectively. The paper emphasizes the importance of network depth, showing that removing middle layers degrades performance, and introduces key techniques like data augmentation (via label-preserving transformations and PCA-based color/brightness adjustments), overlapping pooling, and dropout to combat overfitting. The authors also leverage ReLU activations for faster training and employ a two-GPU parallelization scheme to scale the model. The blog post underscores the paper's foundational role in advancing deep learning for computer vision.
paper_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
paper_abstract: We trained a large, deep convolutional neural network to classify the 1.2 million high-resolution images in the ImageNet LSVRC-2010 contest into the 1000 different classes. On the test data, we achieved top-1 and top-5 error rates of 37.5% and 17.0% which is considerably better than the previous state-of-the-art. The neural network, which has 60 million parameters and 650,000 neurons, consists of five convolutional layers, some of which are followed by max-pooling layers, and three fully-connected layers with a final 1000-way softmax. To make training faster, we used non-saturating neurons and a very efficient GPU implementation of the convolution operation. To reduce overfitting in the fully-connected layers we employed a recently-developed regularization method called “dropout” that proved to be very effective. We also entered a variant of this model in the ILSVRC-2012 competition and achieved a winning top-5 test error rate of 15.3%, compared to 26.2% achieved by the second-best entry.

figures.title: Architecture of the network
figures.caption: The architecture of our network is summarized in Figure 2. It contains eight learned layers — five convolutional and three fully-connected.
